algorithms.name: Convex hull with Andrew's monotone chain
algorithms.explanation: Sorting the points dominates; building the two chains afterwards is linear.

es.explanation: Lo que domina es ordenar los puntos; armar las dos cadenas después es lineal.

algorithms.name: Convex hull with gift wrapping (Jarvis march), h points on the hull
algorithms.explanation: Each of the h hull points is found by scanning all n points.

es.explanation: Cada uno de los h puntos de la envolvente se encuentra recorriendo los n puntos.

algorithms.name: Area of a simple polygon with the shoelace formula
Point in a (possibly non-convex) polygon by ray casting, one query
algorithms.explanation: The ray is tested against every edge.

es.explanation: El rayo se prueba contra todas las aristas.

algorithms.name: Point in a convex polygon by binary search over the fan from one vertex, one query
algorithms.explanation: Binary search finds the wedge that contains the point; then one orientation test decides.

es.explanation: La búsqueda binaria encuentra la cuña que contiene al punto; después decide un test de orientación.

algorithms.name: Closest pair of points by divide and conquer
algorithms.explanation: Two halves, plus a strip in which each point is compared with a constant number of neighbours.

es.explanation: Dos mitades, más una franja en la que cada punto se compara con una cantidad constante de vecinos.

algorithms.name: Testing every pair of n segments for an intersection
algorithms.explanation: There are n(n − 1)/2 pairs, and each test is a constant number of orientation checks.

es.explanation: Hay n(n − 1)/2 pares, y cada prueba es una cantidad constante de chequeos de orientación.

algorithms.name: Diameter of a convex polygon with rotating calipers (h vertices)
algorithms.explanation: Each caliper goes around the polygon once.

es.explanation: Cada calibre da una sola vuelta al polígono.

algorithms.name: Area of the union of n rectangles with a sweep line and a segment tree
algorithms.explanation: 2n events, each updating the segment tree over y in O(log n).

es.explanation: 2n eventos, y cada uno actualiza el segment tree sobre y en O(log n).
